name: Berchicci & King (2022): window of model uncertainty for the SP–FP link
citation: Berchicci, L., & King, A. A. (2022). Building knowledge by mapping model uncertainty in six studies of social and financial performance. Strategic Management Journal, 43(7), 1317–1343. https://doi.org/10.1002/smj.3374
note: Paraphrased from Section 3.1 ('The window of model uncertainty') and Figure 1 of the published article. The authors identify five prominent modelling differences across six quasi-replications of Waddock & Graves (1997); the sample period is a sixth, which they fix for the main analysis. The product of options gives 5,760 models, 3,680 after removing redundant specifications. Use this list as the reference (R) in step 5 to benchmark what the AI finds in the six papers.
studies: Waddock, S. A., & Graves, S. B. (1997). The corporate social performance–financial performance link. Strategic Management Journal, 18(4), 303–319.
McWilliams, A., & Siegel, D. (2000). Corporate social responsibility and financial performance: Correlation or misspecification? Strategic Management Journal, 21(5), 603–609.
Hillman, A. J., & Keim, G. D. (2001). Shareholder value, stakeholder management, and social issues: What's the bottom line? Strategic Management Journal, 22(2), 125–139.
Hull, C. E., & Rothenberg, S. (2008). Firm performance: The interactions of corporate social performance with innovation and industry differentiation. Strategic Management Journal, 29(7), 781–789.

Barnett, M. L., & Salomon, R. M. (2012). Does it pay to be really good? Addressing the shape of the relationship between social and financial performance. Strategic Management Journal, 33(11), 1304–1320.
Zhao, X., & Murrell, A. J. (2016). Revisiting the corporate social performance–financial performance link: A replication of Waddock and Graves. Strategic Management Journal, 37(11), 2378–2388.

reference.description: Outcome variable: accounting measure of financial performance (return on assets) vs market measure (market value added / market-to-book)
Predictor construction from KLD: expert-weighted scale (Waddock & Graves)
Predictor construction from KLD: topics weighted by number of measures (Hull & Rothenberg)
Predictor construction from KLD: two sub-scales, stakeholder management and social issue participation (Hillman & Keim)
Predictor construction from KLD: unitary (equal) weights across measures (Barnett & Salomon)
Predictor construction from KLD: binary indicator of inclusion in the Domini Social Index (McWilliams & Siegel)
Functional form: moderation by firm R&D intensity and industry advertising intensity (interaction terms) (Hull & Rothenberg)
Level of informative variance: between-firm (cross-sectional) vs within-firm (firm fixed effects with lag structure)
Year fixed effects included or not
Lagged dependent variable included or not
Sample time period (differs across the six studies; fixed to the full panel in the main analysis, relaxed in Appendix S3)
Sample restriction: firms with KLD coverage and Compustat financials (restricted sample used for the model space)
